analysis.title: 2027 US Equity Outlook: The beginning of the middle
key_insights: GS forecasts the S&P 500 will reach 8,700 by year-end 2027, a 17% price gain (18% total return including a 1% dividend yield). This compares with a 21% annualized return over the past four years (120% cumulative since late 2022).

S&P 500 EPS growth is forecast to slow from roughly 30% in 2026 to 18% in 2027 excluding mega-cap tech 'other income' from private investment stakes (11% including it). Growth likely slows further in 2028.

The 8,700 target uses an 18x multiple on haircut consensus 2028 earnings. GS 2027 EPS is similar to consensus, but GS 2028 EPS is about 7% below consensus. GS assumes consensus 2028 estimates move partway to GS's forecast over the next 12 months and converge fully during 2028.

Forward P/E fell 19% in 2026 and sits near its 10-year average of about 18x. GS expects elevated interest rates and AI uncertainty to prevent broad multiple expansion in 2027. Valuation on trend earnings remains close to record highs (CAPE 38x, 90th percentile).

AI capex drove about half of S&P 500 EPS growth in 2026. The impulse should shrink in 2027 as capex growth slows and depreciation builds, and the net impulse turns negative by 2028 even with continued AI spending.

The biggest downside risk is a deterioration in the 2028 earnings outlook. Each $50B of AI capex or 1 pp change in semiconductor margins in 2028 shifts S&P 500 EPS growth by about 1 pp. If consensus EPS fell to the 30-year trend and P/E to 17x, the S&P 500 would fall about 25% to roughly 5,600.

The upside case is a P/E rising back to the 10-year average of 19x on confidence in 2028 consensus. The S&P 500 would then end 2027 at 9,400 (+27% from the current level). Triggers include AI productivity, a stronger-for-longer capex cycle, or lower oil prices and interest rates.

Earnings growth is concentrated. The top 10 contributors account for two-thirds of consensus 2027 S&P 500 EPS growth, and NVDA alone for nearly 25%. AI infrastructure stocks have contributed nearly 50% of the S&P 500 return since late 2022, with NVDA at 10%.

Theme 1, the AI relay race: the AI trade should shift from infrastructure to monetization and adoption beneficiaries, including hyperscalers. GS expects hyperscaler capex growth to slow from 105% in 2026 to 73% in 2027 and says the best returns for AI infrastructure stocks are likely behind us.

AI infrastructure stocks have sold off sharply in recent weeks, and semiconductor prices imply a substantial EPS decline. GS says this sets a low bar for a short-term bounce, but sustained outperformance needs confidence in 2028 and beyond earnings, which is unlikely soon.

Hyperscalers show monetization signs. Cloud revenue growth for AMZN, GOOGL and MSFT rose from 25% in 2024 to 54% in Q3 2026, with $1.8 trillion of announced backlogs. The four largest trade at 22x forward EPS versus a 40x peak in 2020 and a 10-year median of 28x.

Enterprise AI adoption is early. In Q3 2026, 13% of S&P 500 companies quantified AI productivity on a use case and 3% quantified an earnings impact. GS recommends physically-intensive AI productivity candidates (Exhibit 50, 38 stocks) to limit disruption risk.

Theme 2, re-leveraging: hyperscaler capex exceeded operating cash flow in Q3 and consensus has free cash flow falling further in 2027. GS credit strategists expect US IG and HY issuance of $2.8 trillion in 2027, up from $2.4 trillion in 2026. Hyperscalers carry about $3 trillion of lease and purchase commitments. The S&P 500 buyback yield is 1.4%, the lowest in two decades outside recessions.
GS expects 'buyback aristocrats' (Exhibit 51) to outperform. They have historically done best when growth decelerates and trade at a 2% P/E premium to the equal-weight S&P 500.

Theme 3, Value in Growth: decelerating growth has historically favored momentum, upward revisions and quality. Valuation dispersion is at a 10-year low, and the Growth factor ranks in the 11th percentile of valuation versus the past decade. Energy infrastructure is a rare area of accelerating 2027 earnings, and Transports are a cyclical option for a macro upside scenario.

Theme 4, Safety in diversification: Health Care and Consumer Staples earnings are modestly below trend with undemanding multiples on trend earnings. They have recently been inversely correlated with the AI trade. GS analysts favor biopharma, parts of managed care, beauty, energy drinks and nicotine.
The S&P 400 mid-cap index trades at 14x forward P/E and 16x trend earnings, a large discount to the S&P 500, and its earnings are slightly below trend.

Late-cycle warning signs: GS notes the Fed hiking cycle is under way and economists expect it to continue through early 2027. The AI boom has become reliant on external financing. Net US equity supply is expected to rise in 2027 by the most since 2000, with only 77 US IPOs YTD versus a 25-year median of 105.
Alpha conditions are favorable: there is no speculative mania, returns track earnings outlooks, and dispersion is elevated and breadth improving, which GS says bodes well for stock pickers.

sector_views.rationale: Rare accelerating earnings in 2027 from a secular trend of investment in energy production, transportation and storage, despite expected lower energy prices.
Attractive cyclical exposure if energy and interest rate pressures ease by more than GS expects. Transports have lagged other energy-sensitive cyclicals.
Earnings modestly below trend, undemanding multiple on trend earnings, inversely correlated with the AI trade. Analysts favor biopharma and parts of managed care.
Earnings below trend and discounted valuation. Analysts see the most opportunity in beauty, energy drinks and nicotine.

AI infrastructure returns are likely behind us as capex decelerates, while Info Tech has historically done well in positive but decelerating growth. Focus shifts to monetization and adoption beneficiaries.

earnings_insights: S&P 500 EPS growth forecast (GS): roughly 30% in 2026 slowing to 18% in 2027 excluding mega-cap tech other income, or 11% including it. GS 2027 EPS $415 (+11%) and 2028 EPS $460 (+11%) per Exhibit 2, versus consensus 2028 of $497. GS 2026 EPS is $375 (+36%).
GS 2028 EPS forecast is about 7% below consensus 2028 estimates, and GS expects consensus 2028 estimates to be revised down in a return to the typical pattern.
Consensus 2027 EPS growth contribution (Exhibit 12): NVDA 24%, MU 14%, GOOGL 6%, AVGO 6%, AMZN 4%, MSFT 4%, AMD 2%, MRK 2%, GILD 2%, SNDK 2%. The top 10 total 67%.

Hyperscaler capex (consensus, Exhibit 3): $887B in 2026 (+105%), $1,402B in 2027 (+58%) and $1,543B in 2028 (+10%). GS baseline of $1,529B in 2027 (+73%) and $1,619B in 2028 (+6%) contributes 12pp, 9pp and (5)pp to S&P 500 EPS growth in 2026, 2027 and 2028.
Q3 2026 earnings season: 13% of S&P 500 firms quantified AI productivity on a use case and 3% quantified an earnings effect (examples of earnings quantification: BR, CHRW, NOW, YUM).

macro_indicators.interpretation: A 17% price gain, 18% total return, based on 18x haircut consensus 2028 EPS.
GS economists forecast growth close to trend. Lower energy prices support real consumer income, offset by tighter financial conditions and a smaller fiscal boost.
Down 19% in 2026 and near the 10-year average. GS base case holds it near 18x in 2027.

macro_indicators.indicator: US IG and HY debt issuance
macro_indicators.interpretation: Up from $2.4 trillion in 2026, reflecting AI-related external financing.
Lowest in two decades outside recessions, as capex has displaced buybacks.

macro_indicators.reading: hiking cycle under way, expected to continue through early 2027
macro_indicators.interpretation: GS economists expect further tightening, which supports elevated rates and holds back multiple expansion.

trade_ideas.description: Long a basket of physically-intensive AI productivity candidates (Exhibit 50, 38 Russell 1000 non-tech stocks, e.g. GM, KO, XOM, CVX, UPS, WM, CSX, DAL, DUK)
trade_ideas.rationale: Companies with a large physical presence capture AI productivity gains with lower disruption risk.

trade_ideas.description: Long Buyback Aristocrats (Exhibit 51, e.g. AAPL, JPM, BAC, WFC, C, AMAT)
trade_ideas.rationale: Strong free cash flow and consistent repurchases should outperform as AI spending weighs on buyback growth and when growth decelerates.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight Growth factor, Energy infrastructure and Transports
trade_ideas.rationale: Decelerating S&P 500 earnings favor secular growth and accelerating earnings, and valuation dispersion is tight.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight Health Care and Consumer Staples as diversifiers
trade_ideas.rationale: Earnings are below trend, multiples undemanding, and both are inversely correlated with the AI trade.
Mid-caps trade at 14x forward P/E and 16x trend earnings and are not over-earning.

risk_factors: Deterioration in the 2028 earnings outlook from slower AI investment or rising semiconductor supply compressing margins.
S&P 500 earnings are about 25% above trend, and a reversion to trend with a 17x P/E implies a roughly 25% decline to about 5,600.
Late-cycle dynamics: Fed tightening, concentration, reliance on external AI financing, and the largest net equity supply since 2000.
Earnings concentration: the top 10 contributors drive two-thirds of 2027 EPS growth and NVDA about a quarter.
Semiconductor margins are elevated and vulnerable.
AI adoption may disrupt existing revenue streams, business moats and the labor market.
charts_described: Exhibit 2 shows S&P 500 EPS of $375 in 2026 (+36%), $415 in 2027 (+11%) and $460 in 2028 (+11%) with the YE 2027 price target of 8,700.
Exhibit 8 shows S&P 500 year-end values across P/E and EPS scenarios, with 18x on $415 GS 2027 EPS at 7,500 and 21x on $415 at 8,700.
Exhibit 10 shows hyperscaler capex scenarios for 2026 to 2028: the baseline is $884B, $1,529B and $1,619B, the upside is $884B, $1,700B and $2,000B, and the downside is $884B, $1,000B and $750B.
Exhibit 25 shows year/year cloud revenue growth for AMZN, GOOGL and MSFT rising from 24% in Q1 2024 to 54% in Q3 2026.
Exhibit 12 lists the top 10 contributors to consensus 2027 S&P 500 EPS growth at 67% in total, with NVDA at 24%.
vol_and_positioning: Equity return dispersion is very elevated (Exhibit 19), and valuation dispersion across S&P 500 companies is at its tightest in 10 years.
S&P 500 net leverage has declined but rises when hyperscaler off-balance-sheet liabilities are included (Exhibit 16).

Net US equity supply is expected to rise in 2027 by the most since 2000, including expiring lockups. Household demand was extremely strong in 2026 and remains a key determinant of 2027 market strength.

tension_points.bull_case: Confidence in current consensus 2028 EPS from AI productivity, a stronger-for-longer capex cycle, or lower oil and interest rates lifts the P/E to the 10-year average of 19x, taking the S&P 500 to 9,400.
tension_points.bear_case: If consensus EPS falls back to the 30-year trend and the P/E drops to the 17x 30-year average, the S&P 500 falls about 25% to roughly 5,600. GS's 2028 EPS is 7% below consensus.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A deterioration in the 2028 earnings outlook, such as a $50B cut to AI capex or lower semiconductor margins (each 1 pp of margin or $50B of capex shifts S&P 500 EPS growth by about 1 pp).

tension_points.theme: AI infrastructure stocks after the selloff
tension_points.bull_case: Valuations imply a substantial EPS decline, setting a low bar for a short-term bounce.
tension_points.bear_case: Capex growth is decelerating, semiconductor earnings and margins are above trend, and visibility on 2028 earnings is unlikely soon, so sustained outperformance is unlikely.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Evidence of confidence in 2028 and later earnings for the AI infrastructure complex.
